title: Build a persistent workspace with Phoenix and SmolBox 0.2.0
description: Edit a page, run successive commands, and restart Phoenix without losing the project. A runnable workspace teaches machine, command, and browser lifetimes.
image_alt: Write, run, and return: a retained machine keeps the project across commands and controller restarts.

title: Prepare once, run in a fresh VM with SmolBox
description: Restore prepared guest state for separate disposable executions. A station dataset shows what checkpoints preserve, what they cost, and when a prepared image is enough.
image_alt: Prepare once, restore separately: one approved idle checkpoint supplies the starting state for three independent disposable executions.

title: How much slower is nested KVM? Measuring our SmolBox lab
description: A reader asked about nested virtualization overhead. Six paired tests showed why startup, guest execution and cleanup need separate clocks.
image_alt: Same workload, different waits: a comparison of direct and nested KVM execution in the SmolBox lab.

title: Controlled network access for disposable VMs in Elixir
description: Fetch a public dataset from a disposable Python VM, collect the report in Elixir, and keep its approved network policy with the execution. A working SmolBox 0.1.3 example.
image_alt: Approve the destinations, run the job, collect the report: an Elixir application gives a disposable VM an explicit outbound network policy.

title: From a full disk to an upstream fix
description: A cleanup failure in our Elixir integration, a fix from smolvm's maintainer, and the tests that closed the loop. A small story of contributing to open source.
image_alt: From a full disk to an upstream fix: reproduce the failure, fix the deletion order, and verify cleanup and the next execution.

title: When the sandbox fails: testing SmolBox with nested KVM
description: What disk exhaustion, worker OOM and a frozen VM taught us about resource limits, execution records and recovery in an Elixir application.
image_alt: When the sandbox fails: a Linux host supervises a disposable worker environment running SmolBox and nested smolvm machines.

title: Introducing SmolBox: managing smolvm executions from Elixir
description: Why we chose smolvm and how SmolBox manages execution identity, outcomes, and cleanup from Elixir, with a runnable Python example.
image_alt: An Elixir application submits an identified command to SmolBox, which manages a smolvm worker and a disposable Python VM.
